html: We released the report and resource of the LLMJudge challenge 🌙! Paper / Website
JudgeBlender has been highlighted in the Microsoft Research Focus blog series. ⭐️
SynDL and LLMJudge have been accepted at TheWebConf (formerly known as WWW) 2025.
I have officially started as a research scholar at the Alan Turing Institute, working on understanding the capabilities of foundation models as part of fundamental research in data science and AI.

title: Research highlighted as innovation on Thomson Reuters website! 🎉
html: My internship work at Thomson Reuters Labs is featured as an innovation on their website!
My blog post on The Rise of Large Language Models in Automatic Evaluation: Why We Still Need Humans in the Loop is now online on the Thomson Reuters Labs Medium channel! [Link]
I gave a lecture, Basics of LLMs and their Safety, at UCL (Data Science for Crime Scientists)! Slides

I have been awarded the prestigious doctoral enrichment placement by The Alan Turing Institute. I will be focusing on understanding the capabilities of foundation models and LLM evaluation. UCL AI Centre News ✨
Our work, SynDL, has been featured in the Microsoft Research Focus blog series. 🥳
We are happy to release our large-scale synthetic test collection for passage retrieval evaluation: SynDL is out! Website / GitHub
Serving as PC for FAccTRec ’24 and SURE ’24.
Check out our LLM4Eval report: Report on the 1st Workshop on Large Language Model for Evaluation in Information Retrieval (LLM4Eval 2024) at SIGIR 2024
Our paper on the role of user profile in the personalization of LLMs is out!
The LLMJudge challenge is officially launched! The challenge aims to explore an alternative approach by using LLMs to generate relevance judgments. Website / GitHub
Serving as PC for ACL and EMNLP 2024 🤗

Can we build a reliable synthetic test collection for evaluation? To answer this question please check our recent paper on the construction of fully synthetic test collections for IR evaluation, accepted by SIGIR ’24 🥳.
Serving as PC for SIGIR 2024 and RecSys 2024 😄
Gave a talk at the University of Gonabad on An Intro to AI: From Traditional ML to LLMs.
Our paper on multi-stakeholder fairness, A Personalized Framework for Consumer and Producer Group Fairness Optimization in Recommender Systems, has been accepted by ACM TORS 🎉
Our full paper on user satisfaction in asking clarification questions accepted by EACL 2024 🎯
Serving as PC for LTEDI@EACL ’24.
The LLM4Eval workshop proposal has been accepted to SIGIR 2024 🥳! The main focus of LLM4Eval is utilizing the capabilities and responsibilities of LLMs for evaluation in IR.
I presented a tutorial on Fairness in Recommender Systems for MSc students of the Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development course at UCL. Check the GitHub repository.
Our team ranked 1st in TREC iKAT 2023 🥇🎉. We submitted Retrieve-then-Generate and Generate-then-Retrieve models, combining LLMs and search for conversational search.

I attended The Text Retrieval Conference (TREC) 2023 as part of the Deep Learning Track organisers and presented our findings on using synthetic queries to build test collections. Website / Paper / Slides
We are organising WITalk, a seminar series that invites researchers to present, share and discuss their research findings in IR and NLP, at the UCL AI Centre.
I delivered a presentation at the CS Reading Group at Qazvin Islamic Azad University (QIAU) on Fairness and Bias in Recommender Systems.
Our survey paper on Asking Clarification Questions (ACQSurvey) accepted at ACL 2023 Main Track! See the publications page.
Serving as PC for RecSys ’23 and ICTIR ’23.
I gave a talk at the DEFirst Reading Group at Mila x Vector Institute on Generalizability of User Fairness in Recommender Systems.
I attended the UCL AI Centre Hackathon.
Serving as PC for SIGIR ’23 and EWAF ’23. 😄
Joining the WI Group at UCL as a PhD student. ✨
Our team, UCL-WI-Group, won the research prize at the IGLU challenge for providing novel solutions!
Two full papers accepted at Bias@ECIR ’22! See the publications page.
